diagnosis: Generated descriptions consistently assume the next news will continue the same geopolitical or corporate conflict narrative (e.g., Nexperia dispute, automaker chip shortages) even when true news shifts to unrelated topics (e.g., Taiwanese financial results, school policy, rare-earth licenses, or human-interest stories). The tone overly anchors on the preceding crisis, predicting escalation or sustained disruption, while true news often introduces positive, mixed, or entirely different developments.
suggestions: Do not assume that the next effective-date news will continue the dominant conflict or crisis narrative from the recent historical window; the story may pivot to an unrelated topic, a parallel development, or a moderately positive industry update.

When the historical trajectory shows no clear next step (e.g., a hearing without ruling, a canceled meeting without substitute), describe a broad range of possible directions—including neutral, mixed, or completely new themes—rather than anchoring on escalation or prolonged deadlock.
